title: Pytheas of Massalia to Britain and Thule, c. 325 BC
summary: A Greek geographer sails from Massalia, past the Pillars of Heracles and up the Atlantic coast to Cornwall; round Britain, to the Thule of the midnight sun and the frozen sea, and to the amber coast of the North Sea. His book is lost, and survives only as quoted by Strabo, Pliny and others, some of whom disbelieved him.

events.label: Belerion, the tin coast of Cornwall
events.text: Pytheas of Massalia (Marseille) reached the tin coast of Cornwall and found the people friendly. Diodorus says they carried the tin out at low tide to an island, which some identify with St Michael's Mount, to sell it to traders.

events.label: Thule, six days north of Britain (place disputed)
events.text: Pytheas reported a land six days north of Britain where in summer the sun hardly set, and beyond it a sea that was neither land nor water nor air, like a sea lung, on which one could neither walk nor sail: sea ice, perhaps. Thule may be Iceland, Norway or Shetland. Strabo thought him a liar.
